question: True or false: some late-Gothic German wooden altarpieces were delivered deliberately unpainted?
answer: True. From about 1490 carvers such as Tilman Riemenschneider delivered limewood altarpieces with only a thin, tinted glaze, letting the carving carry the image. His Münnerstadt altarpiece was finished bare in 1492; a dozen years later the parish had Veit Stoss paint it. The later colour, not the bare wood, was the alteration.
move: Correct an old mistake without overcorrecting into a new one.
ask: After I correct an old mistake, am I now overcorrecting into a new one?
trap: Having learned old sculpture was painted, assuming all of it was.
reference: Michael Baxandall, The Limewood Sculptors of Renaissance Germany, Yale University Press, 1980
